newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Steel, Yang Ming in $4 mln shipping venture.
newsitem.headline: China Steel, Yang Ming in $4 mln shipping venture.

text.p: China Steel Express Corp, a subsidiary of Taiwan steel giant China Steel Corp, said on Thursday it has agreed to set up a US$4.0 million shipping venture with Yang Ming Marine Corp.

"China Steel Express and Yang Ming have agreed to jointly set up a shipping company, using rented bulk carriers in initial operation for international routes," Chen Yuan-cheng, China Steel Express chairman, told Reuters.
Chen, who is also executive vice-president of China Steel, said China Steel Express would take a 70 percent stake in the venture and Yang Ming would own the rest.
The new venture will use 66,000-dead weight tonne Panamax-class and 140,000-dwt cape-size bulk carriers to ship raw materials and goods on international routes, Chen said.
"Other details need further discussion in order to be finalised," he added.
China Steel Express was founded in early 1996 to import raw materials needed by China Steel.
It now has four ships, each with a capacity of 140,000 dwt, and has ordered three more 130,000-dwt carriers, scheduled to be delievered in 1997.
China Steel, previously state-owned, was privatised in April 1995 after its state stake was cut to 47.2 percent.
Yang Ming was privatised in February 1996 after its state stake was reduced to 48 percent.
